title: Pseudo-coherent algebraic effectivity of normalized finite reductions
statement: Let $C$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $J\subset C$ an ideal, and assume $C\simeq\varprojlim C/J^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Suppose $E_n\in D(C/J^n)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] are supplied with transition maps in $D(C/J^{n+1})$ inducing isomorphisms $E_{n+1}\otimes^L_{C/J^{n+1}}C/J^n\simeq E_n$. Assume $E_1$ is bounded above with finitely generated cohomology in every degree. Then $E=R\varprojlim E_n$ [def-weil-derived-limit] is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], and its projections induce isomorphisms $E\otimes_C^L C/J^n\simeq E_n$, compatible with the supplied transitions and quotient cocycles. It is derived $J$-complete, meaning $E\simeq R\varprojlim_n(E\otimes_C^L C/J^n)$. No perfectness of $E_1$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 09AV, lemma-Rlim-pseudo-coherent-gives-complete-pseudo-coherent; Tag 066E, lemma-Noetherian-pseudo-coherent replaces the pseudo-coherence hypothesis by its Noetherian cohomology criterion

proof.text: Put $A_n=C/J^n$ and write $u_n:E_{n+1}\otimes^L_{A_{n+1}}A_n\xrightarrow{\sim}E_n$ for the normalization induced by the supplied transition. The ring $A_1$ is Noetherian: an ideal in $A_1$ is the image of its inverse-image ideal in $C$, hence is generated by the images of finitely many generators. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion] to $E_1$. By [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex] choose a bounded-above finite-free complex $P_1^\bullet$ and $\beta_1:Q(P_1^\bullet)\simeq E_1$; choose $b$ with $P_1^i=0$ for $i>b$.

source.place: Tags 066E and 0CQF, first sentence of proof

proof.text: Inductively suppose $P_n^\bullet,\beta_n$ and the chain transitions up to level $n$ have been constructed. The quotient $A_{n+1}\to A_n$ has kernel $J^n/J^{n+1}$ whose square is zero, since $2n\geq n+1$. By [lem-weil-pbc-pseudo-coherent-nilpotent-invariance], $E_{n+1}$ is pseudo-coherent because $E_n$ is; apply [lem-weil-pbc-nilpotent-marked-free-complex-lift] with $R=A_{n+1}$, this kernel as $I$, $K=E_{n+1}$, $F=P_n^\bullet$, and specified marking $\beta_n^{-1}u_n$. Obtain $P_{n+1}^\bullet$, $\beta_{n+1}$ and $\theta_n:P_{n+1}^\bullet\otimes A_n\simeq P_n^\bullet$, with the same upper cutoff $b$. Let $t_n$ be quotient reduction followed by $\theta_n$. Its derived image represents the supplied transition because the equality for the marking says $\beta_nQ(t_n)$ equals the supplied transition composed with $\beta_{n+1}$. This proves the induction claim and constructs a strict tower representing the original one.

Choose bases of $P_1^i$, of size $r_i$. At each level lift the basis of $P_n^i$ through the surjection $t_n^i$. These lifted vectors are a basis of $P_{n+1}^i$: the resulting map $f:A_{n+1}^{r_i}\to P_{n+1}^i$ is an isomorphism modulo the square-zero kernel; lift its inverse to $g$ using that both modules are free. Both $gf-1$ and $fg-1$ have matrices in that kernel and hence square to zero, so both $gf$ and $fg$ have inverses given by $1-(gf-1)$ and $1-(fg-1)$. Thus $f$ has a left and a right inverse and is invertible. In these compatible bases $t_n^i$ is coordinatewise quotient reduction. Define $P^\bullet=\varprojlim P_n^\bullet$. Completeness [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] identifies $P^i=(\varprojlim A_n)^{r_i}=C^{r_i}$ (finite tuples of compatible coordinates); it also identifies the projection reduction $P^\bullet\otimes_C A_n\to P_n^\bullet$ with an isomorphism of complexes. Differentials commute with this identification by the chain transition equations. The terms vanish for $i>b$.

source.place: Tag 0CQF, finite free terms of the limit; explicit compatible-basis argument

proof.text: Every $t_n^i$ is surjective. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-module-complex-tower-limit] to identify $Q(P^\bullet)$ with a derived limit of the strict tower, respecting projections. The maps $\beta_n$ form a levelwise isomorphism of towers. By [lem-weil-derived-limit-morphism] obtain a morphism of their Roos triangles to the chosen derived limit $E$, and [lem-weil-derived-limit-levelwise-iso] makes its first component an isomorphism $Q(P^\bullet)\simeq E$ respecting every projection. Since $P^\bullet$ is bounded above and finite free, $E$ is pseudo-coherent by [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex].

For scalar extension, regard modules as sheaves on the one-object site with only the identity covering; this merely gives the same module category and termwise tensor. Free modules are flat, since tensor with a free module is a direct sum of copies of the original module, and finite sums preserve exact sequences. Thus $P^\bullet$ is K-flat by [lem-pc-kflat-closure], and [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] computes $E\otimes_C^L A_n$ as $P^\bullet\otimes_C A_n$. The chain isomorphism of step 3 and $\beta_n$ give the asserted isomorphism to $E_n$. To check the projection-induced map, use the ordinary scalar-extension/restriction adjunction of [def-pod-ring-scalar-extension], with $M\to\operatorname{Res}_n(A_n\otimes_C M)$ given by $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. Restriction of scalars is exact because kernels and cokernels are the same underlying modules, so [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor] computes its right derived functor termwise on every complex. Scalar extension has its everywhere-defined left derived functor by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Apply the canonical bijection of [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general] to this adjoint pair, with source module category $\operatorname{Mod}(A_n)$ and target $\operatorname{Mod}(C)$. Its representative formula identifies the adjunct of the chain map $q_n:P^\bullet\otimes_C A_n\to P_n^\bullet$ with the quotient projection $P^\bullet\to P_n^\bullet$: $x$ is sent to $q_n(x\otimes1)$. Naturality through the isomorphism of step 4 and the marking $\beta_n$ identifies the adjunct of $\beta_nQ(q_n)$ with the given projection of $E$. Thus the isomorphism just constructed is exactly the projection-induced map asserted in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0CQF, last sentence; K-flat scalar extension as in Tags 06YT and 06YY; sites-modules.tex, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict (ordinary adjunction); derived.tex, Tags 015F and 0DVC (exact restriction and canonical derived adjunction)

proof.text: Write $q_n:P^\bullet\otimes_C A_n\to P_n^\bullet$ for the chain isomorphisms. For every $m\geq n$ the composite $P^\bullet\to P_m^\bullet\to P_n^\bullet$ equals the projection $P^\bullet\to P_n^\bullet$, coordinate by coordinate. Hence $t_{m,n}q_m$ equals $q_n$ after the coefficient quotient; all quotient cocycles are these strict equations. They remain equations in the derived category and, through the markings of step 2, are precisely the supplied tower equations. The reductions of $E$ are consequently an isomorphic inverse system to $(E_n)$. Applying [lem-weil-derived-limit-morphism] and [lem-weil-derived-limit-levelwise-iso] to this system isomorphism identifies its derived limit with $E$. Thus $E\simeq R\varprojlim_n(E\otimes_C^L C/J^n)$, the derived completeness required in the statement.
